beats: Hook: a big model writing one word at a time is mostly waiting; let a small model guess the next five words and the big one just check (line_spec_editor_waiting, then line_spec_handoff, the cover). Cast for all of L08: the editor = the big target model, the intern = the small draft model.

Why checking is nearly free (slide 30): at batch 1 decoding is matrix-vector work and the GPU's compute sits idle, so checking five words costs about as much as writing one (line_spec_oven_one_cookie vs line_spec_oven_full_tray).
Roots (slide 3): blockwise parallel decoding (Google Brain, 2018) and speculative execution in CPUs: do the likely thing early, undo it if wrong (line_spec_waiter_usual).

Core (slides 4-5): two papers, 2022-23: a small draft model writes ahead, the large target checks the whole draft in one pass (line_spec_intern_drafts, line_spec_editor_checks); T5-XXL 11B with T5-small 60M, Chinchilla 70B with a 400M draft.
Keep the longest correct prefix; the first wrong guess is replaced by the editor's own word, so every pass gains at least one word (red pen ticks and a cross on line_spec_editor_checks).

Sampling, not only greedy (slide 6): accept a draft word with probability min(1, target/draft), else resample from the leftover max(0, target - draft); the result is exactly the big model's own distribution (line_spec_play_or_study for "I like playing / studying"; reuse line_dice_hand; line_spec_twin_books for "exactly the same output").
Speed-ups depend on the task (slide 7): predictable code vs free-form summaries (line_spec_fence_vs_book; reuse line_coder_storyteller).
Takeaway: the same answer with fewer slow passes; the serving season starts here.

drawings.name: line_spec_editor_waiting
drawings.prompt: The editor, a big, calm, older invented man (simple round face, dot eyes, a short bushy beard, half-moon reading glasses, a cardigan with elbow patches), sits in a large armchair at a huge, almost empty desk, chin propped on one hand, drumming the fingers of the other hand on the desk, bored, waiting; on the vast desk lie only one tiny blank card and a fountain pen. On the wall behind him a plain round clock with no hands and no numerals. Square image 1024x1024; the editor and the desk fill about 85% of the width and about 80% of the height. No text, no letters, no numbers.

drawings.name: line_spec_oven_full_tray
drawings.prompt: The very same huge commercial bakery oven as in the first attached image, drawn again exactly the same way: same outline and proportions, the same control strip with two round knobs and three small round lights, the same side racks, the same big door wide open and the same framing, seen from the front. The only change: the enormous baking tray inside is now completely full of neat rows of small round cookies, about eight across and five deep, edge to edge, each cookie a simple circle with a few small dots, the same cookie as the single one in the first image. Square image 1024x1024; the oven fills about 85% of the width and about 80% of the height, centred, exactly like the first image. No dials with numerals. No text, no letters, no numbers.
drawings.refnote: The first attached image is the matching picture of the same oven holding one cookie: copy that oven exactly (shape, controls, racks, open door, framing, line weight) and change only the tray contents. The second attached image is a style reference only (a line drawing made earlier for this series): match its line weight and pen feel, not its content.

On the right, the editor, a big, calm, older invented man (simple round face, dot eyes, a short bushy beard, half-moon reading glasses, a cardigan with elbow patches), sits at a large desk and leans forward, peering over his glasses at the strip, a fountain pen raised, ready to check.
